### Goal: WGCNA analysis to check serine synthesis co-expression module

```{r}
library(WGCNA)
options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
allowWGCNAThreads()
```

```{r}
#using ScanB data
expr_basal_matrix <- read.csv("counts_scanb_basel.csv",row.names = 1)
```

```{r}
# 1. Samples as rows, genes as columns
datExpr <- t(expr_basal_matrix)
datExpr <- datExpr[, !duplicated(colnames(datExpr))]
cat("Start:", nrow(datExpr), "samples x", ncol(datExpr), "genes\n")
```

```{r}
# 2. Remove genes that are mostly undetected (the floor in this data is about -3.32)
detected <- colMeans(datExpr > -3) > 0.5
datExpr <- datExpr[, detected]
cat("After detection filter:", ncol(datExpr), "genes\n")
```

```{r}
# 3. Keep the 5000 most variable genes (MAD), and always keep the genes you care about
key <- c("PHGDH", "PSAT1", "PSPH", "MTHFD1L", "MTHFD2", "SHMT2", "SFXN1", "SFXN2",
         "ATF4", "ASNS", "MKI67")
mads  <- apply(datExpr, 2, mad)
top   <- names(sort(mads, decreasing = TRUE))[1:5000]
keep  <- union(top, intersect(key, colnames(datExpr)))
datExpr <- datExpr[, keep]
cat("Final:", ncol(datExpr), "genes\n")
cat("Key genes present:", intersect(key, colnames(datExpr)), "\n")
cat("Key genes missing:", setdiff(key, colnames(datExpr)), "\n")

```

```{r}
# 4. Standard WGCNA quality check
gsg <- goodSamplesGenes(datExpr, verbose = 3)
if (!gsg$allOK) datExpr <- datExpr[gsg$goodSamples, gsg$goodGenes]
```

```{r}
# 5. Sample outliers: look at the tree
sampleTree <- hclust(dist(datExpr), method = "average")
plot(sampleTree, main = "Sample clustering (Basal, SCAN-B)", labels = FALSE, sub = "", xlab = "")
```

```{r}
# 6. Choose the soft-thresholding power (signed network)
powers <- c(1:10, seq(12, 20, 2))
sft <- pickSoftThreshold(datExpr, powerVector = powers,
                         networkType = "signed", verbose = 5)
fit <- sft$fitIndices
fit$SFT.R.sq <- -sign(fit[, 3]) * fit[, 2]          # signed R^2, the usual criterion
print(fit[, c("Power", "SFT.R.sq", "mean.k.")])

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(fit$Power, fit$SFT.R.sq, type = "n", xlab = "Soft threshold (power)", ylab = "Scale-free fit (signed R^2)")
text(fit$Power, fit$SFT.R.sq, labels = fit$Power, col = "red"); abline(h = 0.80, col = "red")
plot(fit$Power, fit$mean.k., type = "n", xlab = "Soft threshold (power)", ylab = "Mean connectivity")
text(fit$Power, fit$mean.k., labels = fit$Power, col = "red")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
# WGCNA needs its own correlation function; this avoids a name clash with stats::cor
cor <- WGCNA::cor

net <- blockwiseModules(
  datExpr,
  power = 6, networkType = "signed", TOMType = "signed",
  minModuleSize = 30, mergeCutHeight = 0.25,
  maxBlockSize = 6000,                 # one block, since there are about 5000 genes
  numericLabels = TRUE, pamRespectsDendro = FALSE,
  saveTOMs = FALSE, verbose = 3
)
cor <- stats::cor                       # restore

moduleLabels <- net$colors
moduleColors <- labels2colors(moduleLabels)
cat("\nModule sizes:\n"); print(sort(table(moduleColors), decreasing = TRUE))
cat("Genes in the grey (unassigned) module:", sum(moduleColors == "grey"), "\n")

# Where do the key genes land?
key <- intersect(c("PHGDH", "PSAT1", "PSPH", "MTHFD1L", "MTHFD2", "SHMT2",
                   "SFXN1", "SFXN2", "ATF4", "ASNS", "MKI67"), colnames(datExpr))
print(data.frame(gene = key, module = moduleColors[match(key, colnames(datExpr))]))

# Scores for serine and proliferation (same gene sets as before), per sample
zmean <- function(genes) {
  g <- intersect(genes, colnames(datExpr))
  rowMeans(scale(datExpr[, g, drop = FALSE]))
}
ser <- zmean(c("PHGDH", "PSAT1", "PSPH"))
pro <- zmean(c("MKI67", "TOP2A", "MCM2", "PCNA", "CCNB1", "AURKA", "BIRC5", "CDK1"))

# Module eigengenes and their correlation with those scores
MEs <- orderMEs(moduleEigengenes(datExpr, moduleColors)$eigengenes)
tab <- data.frame(module = sub("^ME", "", colnames(MEs)),
                  n_genes = as.integer(table(moduleColors)[sub("^ME", "", colnames(MEs))]),
                  rho_serine = round(sapply(MEs, function(m) cor(m, ser, method = "spearman")), 2),
                  rho_prolif = round(sapply(MEs, function(m) cor(m, pro, method = "spearman")), 2))
print(tab[order(-abs(tab$rho_serine)), ])

# Members of the module(s) that contain the serine genes, ranked by module membership (kME)
mods <- unique(moduleColors[match(intersect(c("PHGDH", "PSAT1", "PSPH"), colnames(datExpr)), colnames(datExpr))])
for (m in mods) {
  idx <- which(moduleColors == m)
  kME <- cor(datExpr[, idx], MEs[[paste0("ME", m)]], use = "p")[, 1]
  cat("\nModule", m, "-", length(idx), "genes. Top 30 by kME:\n")
  print(head(sort(round(kME, 2), decreasing = TRUE), 30))
}

# Save for the next step
write.csv(data.frame(gene = colnames(datExpr), module = moduleColors),
          "scanb_basal_wgcna_modules.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

- **Between subtypes:** about four fifths of the Basal-vs-Luminal serine gap is not explained by proliferation, hypoxia, MYC or ATF4 scores.

- **Within Basal tumors:** tumors with more serine synthesis expression are also the more proliferative ones, and they co-express with the cell-cycle genes.

**What correlates with serine after removing proliferation?**

```{r}
# datExpr, ser, pro already exist from the WGCNA steps
gene_res <- apply(datExpr, 2, function(g) resid(lm(g ~ pro)))
ser_res  <- resid(lm(ser ~ pro))

r <- cor(gene_res, ser_res, method = "spearman")[, 1]
r <- r[!(names(r) %in% c("PHGDH", "PSAT1", "PSPH"))]
r <- sort(r, decreasing = TRUE)

cat("Top 40 genes tracking serine after removing proliferation:\n"); print(round(head(r, 40), 2))
cat("\nMost negative 15:\n"); print(round(tail(r, 15), 2))
cat("\nWhere the programs land:\n")
print(round(r[intersect(c("ATF4", "ASNS", "MTHFD1L", "MTHFD2", "SHMT2", "GPT2", "SFXN1", "SFXN2", "MKI67"), names(r))], 2))

write.csv(data.frame(gene = names(r), partial_rho = r), "scanb_basal_serine_partial_rho.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# what do the top genes do? (GO biological process, universe = the genes in the analysis)
library(clusterProfiler); library(org.Hs.eg.db)
ego <- enrichGO(gene = names(head(r, 150)), universe = names(r), OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db,
                keyType = "SYMBOL", ont = "BP", pAdjustMethod = "BH", qvalueCutoff = 0.05)
print(head(as.data.frame(ego)[, c("Description", "GeneRatio", "p.adjust")], 12))
```

- After removing proliferation, the genes that still move with serine are a stress-response and amino-acid-metabolism set (ASNS, CHAC1, ATF4, GPT2, SHMT2, MTHFD2). That agrees with the earlier regression, where ATF4 targets had a coefficient of about 0.29 in both cohorts and hypoxia contributed nothing.

- **MTHFD1L drops to 0.12**, so within Basal its variation is mostly proliferation, which settles the question from earlier. Its elevation relative to luminal tumors (between subtypes) is a separate matter.

- **The negative end** is immune and stromal genes (KLRF1, CR1, CTSG, CXCL12, MPEG1, WDFY4, GIMAP6). Tumors with more non-tumor content have lower serine scores, which is dilution by other cell types, and it matches the earlier result that serine’s link with immune score disappeared after stromal adjustment.

- SFXN1 (-0.09) and SFXN2 (-0.16) go slightly the opposite way to serine within Basal.
